## Natural history notes

A medium-sized native bee characterized by its fuzzy gray to brown body, pale facial markings, and fast, low flight around blueberry flowers in early spring. In Florida, it is found in gardens, farms, pine flatwoods, scrubby areas, and open woodlands where blueberries and suitable sandy nesting soils occur. Females nest individually in the ground and are especially important pollinators of blueberries, using buzz pollination to vibrate the flowers and release pollen more effectively than many generalist bees.
